title: SYSK Selects: How Zero Works
summary: SYSK Selects rerun of the episode about the number zero. Josh introduces it as a selected favorite. The hosts trace zero's history: Sumerian placeholder wedges, Babylonian place-value and abacus, Roman numerals lacking zero, the Indian origin of zero as a number in the fifth century, Arabic transmission and Fibonacci's introduction of Hindu-Arabic numerals to the West, and Maya use of zero in calendars. They cover the Gregorian calendar's lack of a year zero, Cassini's astronomical year zero, zero as an integer and its role in decimals and fractions, zero's arithmetic properties (additive identity, additive inverse, multiplication, division by zero, zero exponent), and zero floor numbering in elevators. Closing segments include a listener mail about coffee blends and a listener's coffee song.

entities.name: The Nothing That Is: A Natural History of Zero

segments.title: Selects intro and opening banter
segments.summary: Josh introduces this SYSK Selects episode, calling How Zero Works a selected favorite. Hosts banter about zero's etymology across languages and Robert Kaplan's speculation about the origin of the symbol.

segments.title: Zero as placeholder in Sumerian and Babylonian numbering
segments.summary: The hosts describe Sumerian clay tablets with diagonal wedges used as a placeholder for a missing digit, the problem of blank spaces, and the place-value column system later used by the Babylonians.

segments.title: Zero's fear and rejection in the West and Roman numerals
segments.summary: The hosts discuss how nothingness was viewed with discomfort, linked to void and chaos in Christian thought, and note that Romans did not use zero in their numeral system, though they briefly used the word nulla.

segments.title: Zero as a number in India and transmission to the West
segments.summary: Zero is described as first conceived as a number in fifth-century India, possibly by Aryabhata, then spreading to Arab nations. Fibonacci, taught by Arabic tutors, introduced Arabic numerals to the West through his book.

segments.title: Maya zero and calendars
segments.summary: The hosts note that the Maya independently used zero, mainly in their calendar, as a base for counting days.

segments.title: Year zero and calendar counting
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the Gregorian calendar having no year zero, which affected millennium celebrations, and how Jacques Cassini's astronomical system placed year zero at 1 BC with negative and positive years around it.

segments.title: Zero as integer and the decimal system
segments.summary: Zero is described as the integer between negative one and one, neither positive nor negative, and as essential to decimals and fractions, enabling precise measurements such as machine parts.

segments.title: Mathematical properties of zero
segments.summary: The hosts cover zero's additive identity, additive inverses, multiplication by zero, why division by zero is undefined with a multiplication-based explanation, and the zero exponent rule.

segments.title: Elevator floor numbering and Ottoman influence
segments.summary: The hosts note that elevators in some countries once conquered by the Ottoman Turks, such as Hungary and Spain, label the ground floor as zero with basements as negative numbers.

segments.title: Further reading and show notes
segments.summary: Hosts recommend the How Stuff Works zero article, an online article titled Zero in Four Dimensions by Hassain Arsham, and Robert Kaplan's book on zero.

segments.title: Listener mail: coffee blends and coffee song
segments.summary: A listener from Edmonton, Alberta writes about coffee blends used by cafes and Starbucks, and shares a coffee song recorded with her coworkers, which the hosts play.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts thank the listener and explain how to send song submissions and contact the show.
